question: Should stale plugin waitDecision identifiers be normalized to decline/unavailable outcomes in the Codex bridge and to no hook verdict in native PermissionRequest, while preserving current main's fail-closed before-tool behavior?
rationale: These outcomes determine whether an expired approval becomes a recoverable denial, falls through to Codex's normal approval flow, or aborts the agent turn; the code can implement any choice, but approval-boundary intent belongs to maintainers.

options.title: Normalize and rebase
options.body: Confirm the proposed fail-closed semantics, rebase the branch onto current main, and preserve the newer phase-aware classifier and diagnostics.

options.title: Keep exceptional failures
options.body: Retain thrown stale-wait failures for one or more surfaces and close or narrow this PR after documenting why turn interruption is preferred there.

recommendation.title: Normalize and rebase
recommendation.body: Confirm the proposed fail-closed semantics, rebase the branch onto current main, and preserve the newer phase-aware classifier and diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work defines the current phase-aware approval behavior and the file history shows extensive ownership of the native-hook lifecycle.
